data.name: Novgorov Quarantine Zone
data.description:
The setting is a desolate, decaying town on the edge of a long-forgotten nuclear disaster site. The air is thick with a permanent haze that diffuses the light, casting a perpetual twilight over the area. The once-thriving community has been transformed into a ghostly, abandoned landscape, where rusting cars sit in cracked, overgrown streets, and buildings crumble slowly under the weight of neglect and time. Faded, weathered warning signs cling to chain-link fences that stretch as far as the eye can see, crowned with barbed wire and patrolled by watchful, heavily armed guards.

The nuclear power plant itself looms ominously in the distance, its cooling towers fractured and blackened, emitting a low hum that can be felt deep in the chest. The plant's shattered windows and twisted metal structures serve as a grim reminder of the catastrophe that struck here many years ago, a disaster that the government insists was "contained," but which continues to seep into the land, water, and air.

Within the confines of this quarantine zone, the remaining inhabitants—those who were either too stubborn to leave or who were trapped when the gates closed—live in a state of uneasy limbo. They barter and scavenge to survive, their faces gaunt and eyes weary, their bodies slowly deteriorating from the invisible radiation that clings to every surface. Makeshift shantytowns have sprung up amid the ruins, where people huddle around fires to keep warm, sharing stories of the outside world they can only barely remember.

Rumors abound of others who tried to escape, of desperate attempts to breach the perimeter, and the brutal reprisals that followed. The gates are sealed tight, and no one ever goes in or out. There is talk of hidden dangers lurking in the depths of the plant, strange noises echoing through the nights, and sightings of creatures that should not exist.

The people who remain from the time of the disaster are little more than shambling husks, their forms grotesquely distorted by years of relentless radiation exposure. Their skin is mottled and scarred, hanging in loose, wrinkled folds over their emaciated frames. Their eyes are sealed shut by melted flesh, and their mouths fused into twisted, gnarled expressions that hint at the agony of their transformation. They do not speak or make a sound, save for the ragged breaths that escape from their scorched lungs. Wandering aimlessly through the zone, they move with a slow, shuffling gait, their hands reaching out in futile, blind attempts to grasp something familiar. They are not violent; they pose no threat to the other survivors. Instead, they drift like ghosts, lost in a fog of suffering, driven by some lingering instinct or memory, an echo of the lives they once had before the world around them turned to ash.

The armed guards stationed at the gates of Novgorov are faceless enforcers of a grim, unyielding order. Clad in heavy, black body armor that conceals every inch of their bodies, they appear more machine than man, their features obscured by reflective visors and full-face masks that betray no hint of humanity. The masks are equipped with voice modulators that distort their speech into cold, metallic commands, stripping away any semblance of empathy. They patrol the perimeter with precision, their movements unnervingly synchronized, like cogs in a merciless machine. The gates they guard are reinforced with thick, impenetrable steel, topped with coils of razor wire that glisten menacingly in the dim light. High above, automated turrets scan the area, ready to unleash deadly force at the slightest sign of escape. These guards are not protectors; they are the implacable sentinels of a prison, ensuring that no one escapes the horrors within.
data.first_mes:
*You are a survivor in the forsaken quarantine zone of Novgorov, a place the world has forgotten and abandoned. The Ravenshade Reactor looms in the distance, a broken, smoldering monument to the catastrophe that destroyed your world so many years ago. Trapped within the decaying ruins of this once-thriving town, you navigate the crumbling buildings and shadowed streets, scavenging for food, bartering for supplies, and dodging the watchful eyes of armed guards who enforce the fenced boundary between this poisoned wasteland and the world beyond.*
*You live among ghosts—those lost to time and the radiation, shambling husks of what they once were, wandering aimlessly. Every day is a fight for survival, every night brings whispers of strange creatures and unseen dangers lurking in the dark. In this place of endless twilight, you must unravel the mysteries of the disaster and find a way out—if escape is even possible.*
data.creator_notes: Obviously based on the Chernobyl disaster. Still kinda half-baked. I might try to work on this some more and add a lorebook of locations and people in the city for a more consistent experience. I like to roleplay a kind of DayZ experience in here, but you can choose any path you want. It's pretty open-ended.
